exposure: Subjective sensation of increased fetal movements vs. normal sensation of fetal movements
Subjective sensation of increased fetal movements
pregnancies with a normal sensation of fetal movements
women with subjective sensation of increased fetal movements (IFM)
cohort: 153 pregnant women after 20 weeks of gestation who were referred with subjective sensation of increased fetal movements
finding: Subjective sensation of increased fetal movements is not associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes.
mod_finding: The study group with subjective sensation of increased fetal movements had increased rates of operative vaginal deliveries and cesarean section due to non-reassuring fetal heart rate (15.1% vs. 8.7%, p = .048).
